thread:
Sam Keller: Heads up — cloud-report flagged an S3 snapshot export that had public-read ACL for ~6m. Object: s3://redwood-prod-snapshots/prod-users-2026-03-19.sql.gz. Alert shows SSE-S3 (no KMS). Can someone oncall triage? Potential data exposure window 2026-03-19T03:12Z -> 03:18Z. @security-oncall @infra-oncall

DeployBot: Alert: S3 ACL change detected. bucket=redwood-prod-snapshots key=prod-users-2026-03-19.sql.gz event=PutObjectAcl actor=backup-service-role time=2026-03-19T03:12:32Z previous_acl=private new_acl=public-read. SSE header: none (SSE-S3). No kms:Encrypt observed in event.

Jenna Li: If it was SSE-S3 then no customer CMK was used — treat as exposed until proven otherwise. First things: check CloudTrail for PutObject/PutObjectAcl and s3:GetObject events in that window, and run S3 Inventory for SSE status. Also check if any restore + download logs exist (VPC flow? presigned URLs?).

Matt O'Connor: I ran a quick CloudTrail lookup: PutObjectAcl by arn:aws:sts::111222333:assumed-role/backup-service-role/backup-runner at 2026-03-19T03:12:32Z. No kms:GenerateDataKey or kms:Encrypt calls linked to that PutObject. Command I used:

```
aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=PutObjectAcl --max-results 50 --start-time 2026-03-19T03:00:00Z --end-time 2026-03-19T03:30:00Z
```

Matt O'Connor: It looks like the backup job uploaded a snapshot without the x-amz-server-side-encryption header and then applied a public ACL. That's a bug in the backup runner.

Sara Cheng: Agree we should assume exposure. Immediate mitigations: 1) revoke backup-runner's iam:PutObjectAcl and iam:PutObjectPermission rights on the bucket; 2) require PutObject to include x-amz-server-side-encryption and x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id via an S3 bucket policy; 3) enable S3 data event logging + CloudTrail insights for the bucket. Proposed bucket policy snippet to enforce KMS encryption: 

```
{
  "Sid": "EnforceKMS",
  "Effect": "Deny",
  "Principal": "*",
  "Action": "s3:PutObject",
  "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::redwood-prod-snapshots/*",
  "Condition": {
    "StringNotEquals": {
      "s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption": "aws:kms",
      "s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id": "alias/redwood-backup-cmk"
    }
  }
}
```

Sam Keller: Action items (assigning verbally here):
- Matt O'Connor: remove iam:PutObjectAcl from backup-runner role + block ACLs on bucket (bucket ACLs disabled via policy).
- Jenna Li: run full inventory for last 30 days to find objects with SSE-S3 and enumerate keys; also look for GET requests in the window.
- Sara Cheng: start incident timeline, notify legal if PII appears, and prepare re-encrypt playbook for objects stored with SSE-S3.

Matt O'Connor: On it. I'll push RBAC change now and post helm/terraform diff. Quick note: we have some older archives moved to Glacier and transitioned with SSE-S3 via lifecycle. Re-encrypt for Glacier objects needs restore->copy workflow or AWS S3 batch operations — will outline options.

Jenna Li: Inventory script I'm running:
```
aws s3api list-objects-v2 --bucket redwood-prod-snapshots --query 'Contents[].Key' --output text | xargs -n1 -I{} aws s3api head-object --bucket redwood-prod-snapshots --key '{}' --query '{Key: Key, SSE: ServerSideEncryption, KMSKeyId: SSEKMSKeyId}'
```
Will paste any matches that show "ServerSideEncryption": "AES256" (SSE-S3) or missing SSE field.

Sara Cheng: For re-encrypt: simplest path is S3 Copy with KMS: `aws s3 cp s3://redwood-prod-snapshots/foo s3://redwood-prod-snapshots/foo --metadata-directive REPLACE --server-side-encryption aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id alias/redwood-backup-cmk` — note this will count as PUT and will require kms:GenerateDataKey permission for the actor. For large sets consider S3 Batch Operations with a Lambda or S3 Replication with KMS options. Also schedule CMK rotation and ensure key policy allows backup service to use GenerateDataKey only when PutObject has the proper encryption header.

Sam Keller: Good. If anyone finds evidence of downloads or external copies, escalate to @security-oncall immediately and file an incident in #incidents. Keep this thread for coordination; paste audit snippets and Terraform/Helm diffs here. We'll follow up on postmortem and remedial timeline once we have inventory results.

Tariq Leung: Looping in infra infra-policy: we should add a pre-flight CI check to the backup job to assert encryption headers and deny jobs that would produce unencrypted objects. Also recommend we add a cloud-config enforcement rule in our guardrails.

Sam Keller: Thanks all — stand by for updates.
